patterns.title: Game and venue
patterns.summary: A baseball game occurs at a baseball-field site associated with a venue and is designated by a source identifier.

patterns.title: Team participation
patterns.summary: Home and away teams participate in a game while their contextual team roles remain distinct from the teams themselves.

patterns.title: Player identity
patterns.summary: Every accepted player participates in the game and bears a team-scoped PlayerRole that the game realizes, including players who remain on the bench; the role participates in an open role stasis.

patterns.title: Game officials
patterns.summary: Umpires and the official scorer bear persistent adjudicator roles that the game realizes and that participate in open role stases.

patterns.title: Available game-official names
patterns.summary: An official's stable identity is independent of whether this response supplies a name; a label is emitted only when MLB provides the name.

patterns.title: Game temporal region
patterns.summary: A game occupies an interval bounded by temporal instants that are designated by timestamp information.

patterns.title: Season and season phase
patterns.summary: A game is an occurrent part of a reviewed season phase, the phase is an occurrent part of its season, and the provider category remains nominal evidence in a versioned Reference System.

patterns.title: Game postponement and schedule revision
patterns.summary: An official MLB declaration consumes an old game Schedule Plan and produces a distinct later Plan for the same game; Calendar Date Identifiers designate canonical Days, while the provider reason remains nominal evidence rather than an asserted weather cause.

patterns.title: Game containment
patterns.summary: Game, inning, half inning, and plate appearance form an explicit occurrent-part hierarchy.

patterns.title: Plate appearance and player acts
patterns.summary: A plate appearance contains a batter act and pitch acts, with batter and pitcher persons participating through contextual roles.

patterns.title: Plate appearance time
patterns.summary: A plate appearance occupies an interval whose first and last instants are designated by timestamps.

patterns.title: Plate appearance start state
patterns.summary: Each plate appearance records its starting out count; every occupied base contributes a runner participant, a base-scoped stasis, the physical Base, and the corresponding Base Site.

patterns.title: Plate appearance result and adjudication
patterns.summary: Every plate-appearance result is a distinct institutional process with an adjudication act, decision, and event record.

patterns.title: Pitch physical chain
patterns.summary: A pitch act precedes a pitch-ball-motion process involving a pitch-scoped baseball and governed by the pitch rule.

patterns.title: Pitch time and record
patterns.summary: A pitch occupies a temporal interval, has timestamped endpoints, and is described by a separate event record.

patterns.title: Replay review core
patterns.summary: A reviewed on-field judgment produces the prior decision and leads to a distinct replay-review act that produces a replay decision; only source-described challenges create a Challenge Act or challenged-review classification.

patterns.title: Replay adjudicated-process contexts
patterns.summary: The reviewed on-field judgment and replay-review act each belong to a distinct institutional process that is the subject of the corresponding decision.

patterns.title: Replay review result and record
patterns.summary: Review-result information describes the relationship between the two decisions, while a source event record is about the full review pattern, an optional challenge, and the final structured outcome.

patterns.title: Replay review result classification
patterns.summary: Review-result information is classified as affirming or overturning from the source review outcome.

patterns.title: Reviewed on-field decision classification
patterns.summary: The reviewed on-field decision is classified as ball, strike, out, or safe when the source supports one of those alternatives.

patterns.title: Replay decision classification
patterns.summary: The replay decision is classified as ball, strike, out, or safe from the final structured source state.

patterns.title: Replay review transition patterns
patterns.summary: Each replay-review act receives one explicit ball-to-ball, strike-to-strike, out-to-out, safe-to-safe, ball-to-strike, strike-to-ball, out-to-safe, or safe-to-out classification when the source supports it.

patterns.title: Called ball adjudication
patterns.summary: A ball process follows pitch motion and contains a judgment that produces a decision used by a call act; ball-in-dirt is a source-supported variant.

patterns.title: Strike adjudication
patterns.summary: Called and swinging strikes share a counted strike judgment and decision pattern while retaining distinct source-specific branches.

patterns.title: Called strike
patterns.summary: A called strike process is followed by an explicit strike call act that consumes the strike decision.

patterns.title: Swinging strike without contact
patterns.summary: A neutral swing act precedes the counted strike process; no distinct successful or unsuccessful swing class is minted.

patterns.title: Batted-ball physical backbone
patterns.summary: Contact and batted-ball motion are distinct physical processes contained in a batted-ball play and involving the ball and bat artifacts.

patterns.title: Foul-ball physical chain
patterns.summary: A swing and contact precede the foul-ball process, while the batted-ball play and event record retain the physical evidence.

patterns.title: Foul-ball adjudication
patterns.summary: The foul-ball process contains a distinct judgment that uses the fair/foul rule, produces a decision, and precedes a call act.

patterns.title: Counted foul strike
patterns.summary: Where the event-local count is unambiguous, a foul contains a separately adjudicated counted strike process.

patterns.title: Foul-tip physical chain and shared identity
patterns.summary: A foul tip follows swing and contact, includes catching, and is one institutional-process individual typed as both foul tip and strike.

patterns.title: Foul-tip adjudication
patterns.summary: The foul-tip process contains a distinct judgment and decision while the event record remains about the adjudication evidence.

patterns.title: In-play out contact
patterns.summary: A swing and contact precede a fair-ball process for an in-play event whose feed call is out.

patterns.title: In-play no-out contact
patterns.summary: A swing and contact precede a fair-ball process for an in-play event whose feed call records no out.

patterns.title: In-play runs contact
patterns.summary: A swing and contact precede a fair-ball process for an in-play event whose feed call records runs.

patterns.title: Bunt contact
patterns.summary: Every supported bunt attempt creates a Bunt Act; only contact-supported attempts precede contact, and only in-play bunt evidence creates a fair-ball process.

patterns.title: Fair-ball adjudication
patterns.summary: A fair-ball process contains a judgment that uses the fair/foul rule, produces a decision, and precedes a call act.

patterns.title: Batted-ball result sequence
patterns.summary: The terminal batted-ball motion and fair-ball classification precede the plate-appearance result, which is contained in the batted-ball play.

patterns.title: Nominal pitch and batted-ball trajectory classification
patterns.summary: A pitch or batted-ball motion is measured by a reusable nominal category ICE in a response-versioned Reference System; no provider coordinate is projected into a world-side Site.

patterns.title: Pitch event-record identifier
patterns.summary: A playId Identifier ICE designates the MLB pitch event-record ICE and carries the source value; the record remains about the real-world pitch and related evidence.

patterns.title: Counted hit results
patterns.summary: Single, double, triple, and home-run result types share a scorer-supported hit judgment and decision while remaining distinct result classes.

patterns.title: Counted out results
patterns.summary: Batted outs, force outs, strikeouts, double plays, and grounded-into-double-play results share an out adjudication overlay.

patterns.title: Fielder's-choice result
patterns.summary: A fielder's-choice result carries its own judgment and decision using the fielder's-choice rule.

patterns.title: Error result
patterns.summary: A field-error result carries scorer-supported error judgment and decision information using the error rule.

patterns.title: Sacrifice results
patterns.summary: Sacrifice-fly and sacrifice-bunt result types share a sacrifice judgment and decision overlay.

patterns.title: Walk result
patterns.summary: A walk is a specific plate-appearance result with a source-supported umpire judgment overlay.

patterns.title: Hit-by-pitch result
patterns.summary: Hit by pitch is a specific plate-appearance result with a source-supported umpire judgment overlay.

patterns.title: Balk result
patterns.summary: A balk result carries an umpire judgment using the balk rule.

patterns.title: Interference result
patterns.summary: A catcher-interference result carries an umpire judgment using the interference rule.

patterns.title: Obstruction rule boundary
patterns.summary: The obstruction rule individual is available, but the active source mapping has no result pattern that safely invokes it.

patterns.title: Persistent fielding, catching, and baserunning roles
patterns.summary: Players bear persistent fielder, catcher, and baserunner roles whose open stases remain distinct from the players and roles.

patterns.title: Runner out
patterns.summary: A baserunning act precedes an out resolution containing an out judgment and decision described by a separate event record.

patterns.title: Runner reaches a base
patterns.summary: A baserunning act precedes an institutional safe resolution with judgment, decision, reached-base artifact, and record; movement.end does not assert physical base touching.

patterns.title: Runner advances between bases
patterns.summary: A baserunning act precedes an institutional safe resolution with judgment, decision, destination-base artifact, and record; movement.end does not assert physical base touching.

patterns.title: Runner scores from an origin
patterns.summary: A baserunning act from a non-base origin precedes an institutional run resolution with judgment, decision, and record; scoring does not by itself assert physical home-plate touching.

patterns.title: Runner scores from a base
patterns.summary: A baserunning act from a base precedes an institutional run resolution with judgment, decision, and record; scoring does not by itself assert physical home-plate touching.

patterns.title: Stolen base and caught stealing
patterns.summary: A neutral steal-attempt act may support a distinct stolen-base process and adjudication; caught stealing retains the attempt without asserting success.

patterns.title: Passed-ball scoring classification
patterns.summary: A passed ball is an institutional scorer judgment, decision, rule, and counted process; the feed does not independently establish a physical pitch-ball control failure.

patterns.title: Wild-pitch scoring classification
patterns.summary: A wild pitch is an institutional scorer judgment, decision, rule, and counted process; the feed does not independently establish a physical pitch-ball control failure.

patterns.title: Uncaught third strike and unresolved source placeholder
patterns.summary: An uncaught third strike contains the strikeout and its own adjudication while MLB's null runner row remains an event record rather than becoming a fabricated physical failure, movement, or resolution.
